about: Clay's head as fitted architectural pieces (see head_sheets.md): an orange face mass, a dark roof shell fitted over it whose back corners continue as the horns, a nose crest on the front of the roof, a hinged jaw, eyes with lids hinged on the canthal axis, and ear frills tucked under the horns. Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side reference; x = Clay's left.

upper_head.note: The orange face mass under the roof. Top line is the measured side silhouette less the roof thickness; lower edge is the upper lip in front and, behind the mouth corner, the cheek's lower edge, which curves in (concave) and then up to end under the ear opening.

lower_jaw.note: Set back under the overhanging upper lip (strong overbite); chin juts forward and down. Its top edge follows the mouth line: low and nearly level to the mouth corner under the eye, then an inward (concave) curve back and up to end under the ear opening.

dark_plate_edge.note: Eave line of the roof: the height (y) its lower edge reaches. At the front the roof covers the muzzle down to the lip; its edge rises steeply in front of the eye, steps up over the eye (the eye sits tucked under the eave), and runs back level to the horns.

eye.note: Round, wide-open eye tucked under the eave. The canthal axis runs from the inner (medial) corner, front-lower, where the pink caruncle sits, to the outer (lateral) corner, back-upper; it rises about 26 degrees toward the back. The corners differ: the inner one is rounded and held open round the caruncle, the outer one closes to a sharp point. The upper margin arcs highest a little toward the inner corner; the lower margin is flatter and dips lowest toward the outer corner. The lids are thick shells with a rounded margin, hinged on the canthal axis.

lids.columns_note: outer/inner_canthus_deg: where the corners sit on the eyeball, measured from the gaze along the canthal axis. open_deg: how far the margin opens from the gaze at mid-eye; skew tilts where it peaks (negative = toward the inner corner); corner_exp near 0.5 keeps the corner rounded, 1 or more closes it to a point.

caruncle.note: Not a bead: a small fleshy teardrop filling the inner corner between the two lid margins, lying on the eyeball, its point toward the corner, its round end toward the iris; pink, partly tucked under the lids.

socket.note: The face is carved into a socket that holds the eye assembly: inside the lids' footprint the skin runs in just under the lid dome, and a rounded rim (the orbital rim under the lid-ring muscle) turns it back out to the face.

horn.note: The horn grows out of the roof: its root is sculpted into the roof plates, which swell up and wrap its base (a smooth union with fillet radius `fillet`), so the roof's top line runs on into the horn's top line. From there it sweeps back and up in a long, nearly straight line, tapering slowly, and curls up only in the last stretch. Smooth, with hairline incised rings.

ear_frill.note: Sits at the back of the cheek under the horn; its top (front) edge rolls over and curves back to meet the underside of the horn.

roof.note: A thin dark underlay fitted over the face; the visible roof is the plates laid on it (roof_plates). Its eave line is dark_plate_edge.

nose_crest.note: Sculpted into the nose plate, not a separate piece: a raised centre ridge on the front of the muzzle above the upper lip, flaring out to each side over a nostril and flattening onto the muzzle at the nostril's outer corner; it joins the muzzle at the front between the nostrils.

anatomy.note: Sculpt from the inside out: bone landmarks first, muscle masses over them, then skin creases where muscles meet or skin folds over something that moves. Every entry says what it is and what it does to the surface. Positions are side-view (z, y); offsets act on the side of the face.

bone.name: cheekbone and zygomatic arch
bone.why: Clay's most distinctive facial line, in every reference: the cheekbone (jugal) ridge starts at the small pit at the eave notch in front of the eye and runs back beneath the eye to the jaw joint below the ear. Lit above, shadowed below: it overhangs, so its lower edge is crisp and its upper side slopes gently up to the lid-ring pad and the eye. It is the floor the eye assembly rests on.

bone.name: postorbital bar
bone.why: Closes the back of the socket, rising from the cheekbone to the brow (the roof's eave). It is the firm wall the upper crease runs along.

bone.name: eye socket
bone.why: The bony orbit between brow, cheekbone and postorbital bar. Eye and fat fill it; the surface only seats slightly so the lids stand clear of the face round the opening.

muscle.name: orbicularis (lid ring)
muscle.why: The ring muscle round the eye that closes it. It makes a soft raised ring framing the lids, longer toward the back corner along the canthal axis; its lower edge is the zig-zag crease and it sits on the cheekbone shelf. (No form raises the skin inside eye.clear_radius, where the lids sit.)

muscle.name: masseter
muscle.why: The jaw-closing muscle from the zygomatic arch down to the jaw: the full rounded cheek above the cream jowl, behind the mouth corner.

muscle.name: lip and snout muscle (levator)
muscle.why: Lifts the upper lip; a gentle fullness on the side of the muzzle in front of the eye, below the roof's eave.

muscle.name: temporalis
muscle.why: Fills the skull behind the eye up to the roof; it is why the cranium under the roof is wide behind the brow. Shaped by the face stations, not a brush.

skin.name: lower lid crease (zig-zag)
skin.why: Where the orbicularis pad meets the cheekbone: measured from the side reference, front-lower to the back corner.

skin.name: upper lid crease
skin.why: The fold where the lid ring tucks under the brow, running back from the eye's back corner along the postorbital bar.

skin.name: masseter fold over the jowl
skin.why: The cheek muscle's lower edge folding over the jowl, parallel to and above the rising mouth line.

skin.name: ear opening
skin.why: The ear opening, just above where the mouth line ends.

skin.name: pit at the eave notch in front of the eye
skin.why: A small pit at the eave notch; not the nostril.

expressions.note: Expression comes from muscles. Each muscle action is a shape of the face (a morph target) plus lid bone turns; an expression is a mix of actions, after the Facial Action Coding System (FACS action units noted). Clay's brow is the rigid roof eave, so brow actions move the skin between eave and lid, and the lids, rather than the plate.

cheekRaise.muscles: orbicularis oculi, orbital part, with zygomaticus major pulling the mouth corner up and back

lipRaise.muscles: levator labii superioris (and alaeque nasi): lifts the upper lip off the teeth and wrinkles the snout

lipCornerDown.muscles: depressor anguli oris: pulls the mouth corner down

browLower.muscles: corrugator and procerus: draw the brow skin down and in toward the inner corner; the skin between eave and upper lid bunches over the eye

innerBrowRaise.muscles: frontalis, inner part: lifts the skin above the inner corner of the eye

expressions.pose_columns: lids: turns in radians of [upper lid inner half, upper lid outer half, lower lid]; positive closes
expressions.muscle_actions_note: blink (orbicularis oculi, palpebral part: AU45) is a shape of the lids themselves, built with them

roof_plates.note: The roof is not one scored sheet: every reference shows distinct plates in consistent rows. A nose plate caps the front of the muzzle (the nose crest sits on it). A top row of wide transverse bands runs over the top of the muzzle and skull from behind the nose plate to the horns. Each side has an edge row of near-square plates along the eave, staggered against the top row; over the eye the edge row narrows to the brow plate under the stepped eave. Plates are solid tiles with rounded edges, each a little thicker toward its back edge and overlapping the next one back, like shingles; the gaps between them are the consistent dark lines of the art.
roof_plates.top_row_note: top row spans face angle pi/2 +- top_half_angle(z); the edge rows run from the eave up to it
